skill.name: image-generator
skill.description: Generate teaching visuals and lesson diagrams through Gemini browser automation, using creative briefs, quality gates, iteration feedback, and organized image placement.
skill.summary: Creates Gemini-generated teaching visuals with structured briefs, quality checks, and lesson-ready organization.
skill.author: 92Bilal26

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command alerts are Markdown code fences or prompt examples and were adjudicated as false positives. The real risks are a local browser-use shell startup command, a Bash-based asset copy step, external Gemini browser navigation, and batch instructions that may suppress user confirmations.

remediation.suggestion: Document exactly what start-server.sh does and require explicit user approval before running it.

remediation.issue: Bash file copy and lesson embedding steps
remediation.suggestion: Constrain writes to the intended project image directories and ask before modifying lesson files.
Warn users that creative briefs and generated images may be processed by Gemini before sending sensitive material.
Clarify that autonomy never overrides tool approval, security prompts, or user-requested review checkpoints.

content.value_statement: Course teams need consistent visuals that explain concepts quickly. This skill turns creative briefs into Gemini image-generation workflows with quality gates and file organization.
actual_capabilities: Guides Gemini image generation from structured creative briefs.
Applies six quality gates for spelling, layout, color, typography, teaching value, and uniqueness.
Supports batch workflows for multiple lesson visuals.
Provides principle-based feedback when a generated image fails review.
Organizes approved images into part and chapter paths.
Creates checkpoint notes for interrupted batches.
limitations: Requires browser-use automation and access to Gemini.
Depends on Gemini availability and output quality.
Not intended for stock photos or decorative images.
Local copy and embed steps require file access and user oversight.

use_cases.title: Create Chapter Illustrations
use_cases.description: Turn lesson briefs into visuals that match learning goals, proficiency level, and visual hierarchy.

use_cases.title: Build Technical Diagrams
use_cases.description: Generate diagrams for architecture, orchestration, workflow, or concept explanations used in teaching material.

use_cases.title: Run Visual Production Batches
use_cases.description: Process many planned visuals with quality checks, retries, placement notes, and final completion summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Generate One Visual
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-generator to create one teaching visual from this brief: [brief]. Verify all six gates before download.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Failed Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-generator to improve the current visual. Gate [number] failed because [issue]. Provide principle-based feedback and retry.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Lesson Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-generator to generate visuals for this lesson list: [items]. Use a new chat for each visual and report completion at the end.

prompt_templates.title: Resume from Checkpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-generator to resume from this checkpoint: [checkpoint]. Continue remaining visuals, update lesson embeds, and summarize deferred issues.

output_examples.input: A creative brief for a Kubernetes orchestration diagram for B1 learners.
output: A Gemini-ready prompt that preserves story, intent, metaphor, colors, and typography.
A pass or fail review across the six quality gates.
A placement note for the approved chapter image.

output_examples.input: A request to generate all visuals for one course part.
output: A per-visual progress summary with generated, deferred, and failed items.
Short feedback notes for any images that needed retries.
A final location summary for the approved image files.

output_examples.input: An interrupted batch checkpoint with completed and remaining visuals.
output_examples.output: A resumed production plan that continues remaining visuals and updates progress after each completed image.

best_practices: Use full creative briefs with story, intent, metaphor, color meaning, and typography hierarchy.
Verify every image against all six quality gates before saving it.
Use separate Gemini chats for separate visuals to reduce context carryover.
anti_patterns: Do not accept the first output without visual inspection.
Do not replace concept briefs with rigid pixel instructions.
Do not run batch downloads or file writes without clear user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It guides creation of teaching visuals, chapter illustrations, and lesson diagrams using Gemini image generation.

faq.question: Does it create images directly inside Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. It uses those tools to guide browser automation and quality review for Gemini image generation.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Structured creative briefs work best, especially briefs with story, intent, metaphor, colors, composition, and typography goals.

faq.question: Can it process many visuals?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes batch guidance for multiple visuals, separate chats, retries, checkpoints, and final status reports.

faq.question: What quality checks does it use?
faq.answer: It checks spelling, layout, color, typography, teaching clarity, and uniqueness before accepting an image.

faq.question: What should users review before using it?
faq.answer: Review Gemini data sharing, browser automation permissions, downloaded files, and any local copy or embed operations.
